//include: raycast-env.d.ts is COMMITTED, not generated on demand. Raycast's own toolchain writes it from the manifest, and a machine without that toolchain — CI, or anybody running only the repository's aggregate typecheck — cannot produce it. Left out of git, `tsc --noEmit` fails there on every getPreferenceValues() call.
//compilerOptions: `module: preserve` (bundler resolution) rather than Raycast's older commonjs/node10 default: TypeScript 6 refuses node10 outright. It is also why the vendoring step rewrites every relative import specifier to drop its `.js` extension — extensionless is the one spelling both this resolver and Raycast's esbuild bundler agree on.
